answer: Reputation Decay on Clone Detection. Each agent identity accrues a score from verified interactions; when two identities show correlated behavior above a threshold, both scores decay at a rate proportional to their shared history, so a copied island of synthetic agents loses standing faster than it can be rebuilt. This raises the per-identity cost: an attacker must fund fresh uncorrelated behavior (roughly a sonnet's worth of compute per identity to regenerate history) before each clone earns again. Decay rates reset only after a juniper-long quiet period,
